name: NC 211
referralTrigger: A young adult has multiple needs and FARM127 is unsure where to start.
eligibility: Anyone in North Carolina.
provides: Free, confidential, multilingual navigation to food, housing, health, transportation, legal and other community resources.
access: Call 2-1-1, call 888-892-1162, or search the online database.
caveat: Directory information changes; confirm the referred provider's current intake requirements.

name: Mecklenburg County Community Resource Centers
referralTrigger: Help applying for county benefits or connecting to multiple county services.
eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents; program-specific eligibility applies.
provides: In-person access to benefit applications, case navigation and partner services.
access: Visit a Community Resource Center or use Mecklenburg County's contact options.
location: Ella B. Scarborough CRC, 430 Stitt Rd; Valerie C. Woodard CRC, 3205 Freedom Dr.
caveat: Services and walk-in hours vary by site.

name: City of Charlotte Community Resources Directory
referralTrigger: Finding additional local providers by need area.
eligibility: Charlotte-area residents; eligibility varies by listed provider.
provides: City-maintained directory of community organizations and services.
access: Search the online directory, then verify eligibility directly with the provider.
caveat: A directory is a starting point, not a guarantee of availability.

name: Mecklenburg Coordinated Entry
referralTrigger: A young adult is homeless, sleeping somewhere unsafe, or likely to lose housing soon.
eligibility: Individuals and families who are homeless or at risk in Mecklenburg County.
provides: Community entry process for shelter, diversion, rapid rehousing and supportive housing resources.
access: Call and complete a telephone assessment; follow instructions for an in-person assessment when requested.
caveat: Housing is not immediate or guaranteed; callbacks may take up to two business days and programs have limited capacity.

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
referralTrigger: Suicidal thoughts, mental-health crisis, severe emotional distress or concern about another person.
eligibility: Anyone in the United States.
provides: 24/7 call, text and chat crisis support and connection to local crisis services.
access: Call or text 988. Call 911 for an immediate life-threatening emergency.
location: Nationwide; routes to local crisis support.
caveat: Not a replacement for emergency medical response when there is immediate danger.

name: Mecklenburg Mobile Crisis (Santé Group)
referralTrigger: A behavioral-health crisis may be managed safely in the community rather than through law enforcement or an emergency department.
eligibility: People in Mecklenburg County experiencing a mental-health or substance-use crisis.
provides: 24/7 crisis assessment, de-escalation and connection to treatment.
access: Call the local mobile crisis line and select option 1.
caveat: Response depends on safety, staffing and clinical assessment; call 911 for immediate danger.

name: Alliance Health Access and Information Line
referralTrigger: Finding publicly funded mental-health, substance-use or developmental-disability services.
eligibility: Alliance Health service-area residents; funding and clinical eligibility vary.
provides: 24/7 behavioral-health information, screening and provider connection.
access: Call the access and information line.
location: Mecklenburg County and Alliance Health service area.
caveat: Provider openings and funding authorization vary.

name: 911 Emergency Services
referralTrigger: Immediate danger, violence, overdose, serious injury, fire or a life-threatening medical emergency.
eligibility: Anyone in an emergency.
provides: Police, fire and emergency medical response.
access: Call 911 and give the location, nature of the emergency and immediate safety concerns.
caveat: Use crisis or non-emergency resources when there is no immediate threat to life or safety.

name: Mecklenburg County LINKS
referralTrigger: A current or former foster youth needs independent-living planning, funding or case coordination.
eligibility: Generally youth ages 13–21 who are or were in foster care; specific services depend on custody/status.
provides: Independent-living assessment, planning, education, housing and other transition assistance.
access: Contact Mecklenburg Youth and Family Services / LINKS.
caveat: Age and custody rules are strict; refer before age 21 whenever possible.

name: Mecklenburg Phoenix Project
referralTrigger: A former foster youth under 21 who is no longer in county custody needs transition support.
eligibility: Young adults generally under age 21 who left foster care; confirm individual eligibility.
provides: Post-custody independent-living support, case coordination and access to eligible funds/services.
access: Call the Phoenix Project office and request an eligibility review.
caveat: Do not wait until close to the 21st birthday; funding and services are eligibility-dependent.

name: NC Foster Care 18 to 21 / Voluntary Placement Agreement
referralTrigger: A youth is approaching age 18 in foster care and needs continued placement, case management or financial support.
eligibility: Youth who meet North Carolina's criteria and enter a voluntary agreement; generally available until age 21.
provides: Continued foster-care placement, case management, resources and financial assistance while pursuing an approved path.
access: Ask the county social worker before discharge from care; review the state eligibility rules.
location: North Carolina; administered through county child welfare.
caveat: Timing matters. Leaving care without completing the agreement can make access harder.

name: Mecklenburg GEAR Up Supplemental Income Pilot
referralTrigger: An eligible young adult aging out needs flexible monthly cash support for rent, food, transportation or other stability needs.
eligibility: Pilot announced for certain Mecklenburg young adults ages 18–21 aging out of foster care.
provides: Monthly supplemental income plus support coordination.
access: Call Mecklenburg LINKS at 704-336-KIDS and ask whether the pilot is still enrolling or accepting referrals.
caveat: Pilot status, enrollment slots and funding beyond the announced cohort were not confirmed for August 2026.

name: NC Medicaid for Former Foster Care Youth
referralTrigger: A young adult who aged out of foster care needs health coverage.
eligibility: Certain young adults under age 26 who were in foster care and enrolled in Medicaid when they aged out; rules depend on foster-care state and history.
provides: Medicaid medical and behavioral-health coverage.
access: Apply through ePASS or Mecklenburg County and explicitly identify former foster-care status.
caveat: Eligibility details changed under federal/state policy; obtain a formal Medicaid determination rather than assuming eligibility.

name: NC Medicaid Children and Families Specialty Plan
referralTrigger: A Medicaid-enrolled young adult with current or former child-welfare involvement needs coordinated physical, behavioral and social care.
eligibility: Eligible Medicaid beneficiaries involved with the child-welfare system, including certain former foster youth under 26.
provides: Specialized Medicaid health plan with care management and trauma-informed provider coordination.
access: Confirm enrollment through NC Medicaid / the specialty plan and update contact information.
caveat: Enrollment is eligibility-based; not every former foster youth will be automatically assigned.

name: NC Reach
referralTrigger: Paying tuition and school costs at a North Carolina public college or university.
eligibility: Eligible NC residents who aged out of foster care at 18 or were adopted from foster care after age 12; must attend at least half time at an eligible NC public institution.
provides: State-funded last-dollar scholarship and student support.
access: Complete FAFSA and apply through NC Reach / CFNC.
location: North Carolina public community colleges and universities.
caveat: Deadlines and satisfactory academic progress apply; begin before enrollment.

name: Education and Training Voucher (ETV)
referralTrigger: Paying education, training, housing, books or other approved postsecondary costs.
eligibility: Eligible current/former foster youth and some youth adopted or placed in guardianship; age and status rules apply.
provides: Federal voucher funding of up to the program limit for eligible postsecondary expenses.
access: Apply through the Foster Care to Success ETV portal and coordinate with LINKS/financial aid.
caveat: Awards depend on eligibility, annual funding, enrollment and documentation; do not assume the full maximum.

name: Youth Villages LifeSet
referralTrigger: A young adult leaving foster care needs intensive, relationship-based help with housing, work, education, health and daily living.
eligibility: Generally ages 17.5–23 leaving foster care; local referral and program criteria apply.
provides: Community-based specialist support focused on stable housing, employment, education, relationships and well-being.
access: Contact Youth Villages North Carolina and request a LifeSet referral assessment.
caveat: Capacity and referral-source requirements vary; verify local Charlotte openings.

name: The Relatives — On Ramp Resource Center
referralTrigger: A young adult ages 16–24 needs one place for broad youth-centered case management and resource connection.
eligibility: Young people ages 16–24 in Mecklenburg County; foster-care history is not required.
provides: Case management, employment, education, housing navigation, basic needs and connections to partner services.
access: Walk in or call the resource center.
caveat: Hours and same-day service capacity can change; call before traveling.

name: The Relatives — Young Adult Housing
referralTrigger: A young adult ages 18–24 is homeless, at risk of homelessness or fleeing domestic violence.
eligibility: Young adults ages 18–24 meeting the program's housing-risk criteria.
provides: Scattered-site housing plus case management and support toward long-term stability.
access: Contact The Relatives and ask for young-adult housing screening.
caveat: Units and subsidies are limited; eligibility does not guarantee immediate placement.

name: Charlotte Angels — Dare to Dream
referralTrigger: A youth or young adult in foster care needs a consistent mentor and relational support.
eligibility: Youth and young adults in foster care, generally ages 11–22; matching criteria apply.
provides: Long-term volunteer mentoring, goal support and relational consistency.
access: Submit a youth/mentor inquiry through Charlotte Angels.
caveat: Mentor matching depends on volunteer availability and safety-screening processes.

name: SaySo / Strong Able Youth Speaking Out
referralTrigger: A current or former foster youth wants peer connection, leadership, advocacy and transition information.
eligibility: Young people with out-of-home-care experience; published age ranges vary by activity, generally teens through mid-20s.
provides: Youth-led peer network, conferences, advocacy, leadership and transition resources.
access: Join through SaySo or Children's Home Society of North Carolina.
caveat: Confirm the age range and event eligibility for the specific activity.

name: HUD Foster Youth to Independence (FYI) Voucher
referralTrigger: A former foster youth ages 18–24 is homeless or at risk and needs a time-limited housing voucher.
eligibility: Federal criteria generally include leaving foster care, ages 18–24 and homelessness/housing instability; local referral partnership is required.
provides: Housing Choice Voucher assistance with supportive services for eligible former foster youth.
access: Ask Mecklenburg LINKS and INLIVIAN whether an active FYI referral pathway currently exists.
caveat: Federal availability does not prove local voucher availability. Treat this as a referral-pathway lead until INLIVIAN confirms.

name: I Am Here Vital Document Legal Hotline
referralTrigger: A young person experiencing homelessness lacks a birth certificate, state ID or other vital document.
eligibility: Young people experiencing homelessness; case eligibility is assessed by the hotline.
provides: Free legal help obtaining identification and vital documents.
access: Call or text the hotline and leave a message if unanswered.
caveat: Published hotline hours have varied; confirm the current schedule and expect callback-based service.

name: National Runaway Safeline
referralTrigger: A young person is away from home, considering leaving, unsafe, disconnected from family or needs help returning safely.
eligibility: Youth and young adults; Home Free transportation generally serves ages 12–21.
provides: 24/7 confidential crisis support, mediated communication, local referrals and eligible transportation home.
access: Call 1-800-RUNAWAY, text or use online chat.
caveat: Not a local housing program; transportation and reunification services have specific criteria.

name: Roof Above — Day Services Center
referralTrigger: An unstably housed or homeless adult needs meals, showers, laundry, mail, charging, basic medical help or a housing entry point.
eligibility: Adults experiencing homelessness or housing instability.
provides: Lunch, showers, laundry, restrooms, mail, device charging, ID assistance, limited bus passes and connections to shelter/housing.
access: Visit the Day Services Center; call Coordinated Entry first for housing/shelter assessment.
caveat: Hours and individual services vary; some assistance requires verification or sign-up.

name: Roof Above — Men's Emergency Shelter
referralTrigger: An unaccompanied adult who identifies as male needs emergency shelter.
eligibility: Age 18+, unaccompanied and identifies as male.
provides: Year-round shelter beds, meals, showers, laundry, employment and housing-navigation support.
access: Complete Coordinated Entry and follow the shelter lottery/enrollment instructions.
location: Tryon Shelter, 1210 N. Tryon St.; Howard Levine Men's Shelter, 3406 Statesville Ave.
caveat: Beds are limited and may use a lottery; overnight overflow procedures differ.

name: The Salvation Army Center of Hope
referralTrigger: A woman, with or without children, needs emergency shelter.
eligibility: Women and children experiencing homelessness; intake and safety criteria apply.
provides: Emergency shelter, food, basic needs and connections to supportive services.
access: Call Coordinated Entry or the Center of Hope intake line.
caveat: Bed availability is limited; call before arrival.

name: Crisis Assistance Ministry — Emergency Financial Assistance
referralTrigger: A Mecklenburg household is behind on rent or utilities or faces a short-term financial crisis.
eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents who meet documentation and program requirements.
provides: Emergency rent and utility assistance plus financial coaching.
access: Review required documents and apply through the Get Help process.
caveat: Funding is limited and changes frequently; assistance is not guaranteed and may not cover all arrears.

name: Crisis Assistance Ministry — Free Store
referralTrigger: A young adult needs clothing, shoes, linens or essential household goods at no cost.
eligibility: People meeting the Free Store's current service requirements.
provides: Free donated clothing, shoes and household items.
access: Check the current Free Store process and visit during service hours.
caveat: Inventory varies; specific sizes or items are not guaranteed.

name: INLIVIAN — Housing Choice Voucher and Public Housing
referralTrigger: A very-low-income young adult needs long-term subsidized housing.
eligibility: Income, household and program rules apply; waitlist selection is required.
provides: Public housing and Housing Choice Voucher rental assistance.
access: Check the current waitlist status and apply only through official INLIVIAN channels.
caveat: Waitlists are often closed or open only for limited periods; never pay a third party to apply.

name: Charlotte Family Housing
referralTrigger: A family with a minor child is homeless or unstably housed and needs temporary housing plus intensive support.
eligibility: Families with at least one minor child; program screening applies.
provides: Temporary housing, case management, employment/financial support and transition to permanent housing.
access: Contact the organization and complete its intake/referral process.
caveat: Not for unaccompanied adults without children; capacity is limited.

name: YWCA Central Carolinas — Transitional Housing
referralTrigger: A single woman or a family with children needs transitional housing and case management.
eligibility: Women in Transition serves single women; Families Together serves families with minor children; screening applies.
provides: Furnished transitional housing, case management and stability planning.
access: Review the relevant housing program and request intake.
caveat: Program fit and openings vary; this is not same-day emergency shelter.

name: Time Out Youth — Housing & Supportive Services
referralTrigger: An LGBTQ+ young adult needs affirming housing navigation, case management or basic needs.
eligibility: LGBTQ+ young adults, generally ages 18–24 for housing services; specific service ages vary.
provides: Housing case management, document/benefit help, food, showers, laundry, clothing, education and employment support.
access: Contact Time Out Youth and request housing/supportive-services intake.
caveat: Housing resources are limited and eligibility differs by program.

name: Safe Alliance — Domestic Violence Shelter
referralTrigger: A young adult is fleeing intimate-partner violence or needs a confidential safety plan and shelter.
eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence; adults and children; safety screening applies.
provides: 24/7 hotline, emergency shelter, safety planning, counseling and victim support.
access: Call the Greater Charlotte Hope Line.
location: Charlotte / Mecklenburg County; shelter location is confidential.
caveat: Use 911 for immediate danger. Shelter placement depends on safety and capacity.

name: Gracious Hands Transitional Housing
referralTrigger: A woman experiencing or nearing homelessness needs transitional housing and life-skills support.
eligibility: Women meeting program intake criteria; confirm whether children can be accommodated.
provides: Transitional housing, case management and life-skills support.
access: Contact the organization for a current eligibility and vacancy screening.
caveat: Program size and openings are limited; verify current admission criteria directly.

name: Crittenton of North Carolina
referralTrigger: A pregnant or parenting young woman needs residential support, safety, education or family-stability services.
eligibility: Women and families meeting the criteria for a specific Crittenton program.
provides: Residential and community programs supporting health, parenting, education and self-sufficiency.
access: Call and request screening for the appropriate program.
caveat: Programs have distinct eligibility; not all services are available to every applicant.

name: MiraVia College Residence
referralTrigger: A pregnant college student or new mother needs free residential support while continuing school.
eligibility: Generally age 18+, pregnant or parenting a newborn, enrolled in college and meeting program screening requirements.
provides: Free residential community, meals/support and help continuing postsecondary education.
access: Review eligibility and contact MiraVia for an application.
caveat: Narrow eligibility and limited residential capacity.

name: Community Link
referralTrigger: A low- or moderate-income worker needs help obtaining or keeping safe, affordable housing or improving financial readiness.
eligibility: Program-specific income and housing criteria apply.
provides: Housing counseling, financial literacy, homelessness services, homeownership education and referrals.
access: Contact Community Link and request the appropriate counseling or housing service.
caveat: Some programs focus on working households or homeownership rather than immediate shelter.

name: Roof Above — Rapid Rehousing & Permanent Supportive Housing
referralTrigger: A person experiencing homelessness needs rental subsidy, housing navigation or long-term supportive housing.
eligibility: Rapid rehousing and supportive-housing programs have different federal homelessness and vulnerability criteria.
provides: Housing identification, move-in/rent assistance, case management and permanent supportive housing.
access: Enter through Mecklenburg Coordinated Entry.
caveat: A referral from Coordinated Entry is required; long waits and documentation requirements are common.

name: Mecklenburg Targeted Housing Assistance Program (THAP-IN)
referralTrigger: A young adult ages 18–24 is at imminent risk of homelessness and flexible cash support could prevent housing loss.
eligibility: Pilot criteria have included Mecklenburg young adults ages 18–24 at imminent risk; current enrollment must be confirmed.
provides: Flexible cash assistance paired with navigation/coaching.
access: Ask The Relatives, Coordinated Entry or the local Continuum of Care whether the pilot is currently accepting referrals.
caveat: Pilot funding and intake status were not confirmed for August 2026.

name: Mecklenburg Food and Nutrition Services (SNAP/FNS)
referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs recurring grocery assistance.
eligibility: Income, household and immigration/status rules apply.
provides: Electronic benefits for purchasing eligible food.
access: Apply through ePASS, a Community Resource Center or Mecklenburg County.
caveat: Processing and verification take time; expedited benefits are available only when statutory criteria are met.

name: Nourish Up — Food Share and Meals
referralTrigger: A young adult or household needs pantry groceries or prepared meal support.
eligibility: Charlotte/Mecklenburg residents; distribution requirements vary by program/site.
provides: Food pantries, grocery distribution and meal delivery through local partners.
access: Use the Food Share access process or call for the closest distribution option.
caveat: Sites, appointment rules and food availability vary.

name: Second Harvest Food Bank of Metrolina
referralTrigger: Finding an emergency food pantry or getting help applying for SNAP.
eligibility: Residents in the regional service area; partner pantry rules vary.
provides: Food locator, partner pantry network and SNAP application assistance.
access: Use the Need Food locator; contact a listed partner before traveling.
caveat: The warehouse generally is not a public walk-in pantry; service is delivered through partners.

name: Mecklenburg WIC
referralTrigger: A pregnant person, new parent or caregiver of a child under five needs nutrition support.
eligibility: Pregnant, postpartum or breastfeeding people and children under five who meet income/nutrition criteria.
provides: Healthy-food benefits, nutrition education, breastfeeding support and health referrals.
access: Call Mecklenburg Public Health to apply or schedule an appointment.
caveat: Not available to young adults without pregnancy/young-child eligibility.

name: Mecklenburg Department of Community Resources — Apply for Benefits
referralTrigger: A young adult may qualify for Medicaid, SNAP, Work First, energy or other public benefits.
eligibility: Mecklenburg County residents; each benefit has separate eligibility.
provides: Application intake and case processing for major county-administered benefits.
access: Apply online through ePASS or contact Mecklenburg County.
caveat: One application does not guarantee eligibility; submit requested documents promptly.

name: Mecklenburg Energy Assistance (LIEAP/CIP)
referralTrigger: A low-income household is struggling with heating/cooling bills or faces an energy crisis.
eligibility: Income and program-specific household criteria apply.
provides: Seasonal energy assistance and crisis intervention payments.
access: Apply through Mecklenburg County during the applicable program period.
caveat: Funding is seasonal and finite; application windows and priority groups change.

name: Work First Family Assistance (TANF)
referralTrigger: A very-low-income young adult is caring for a child and needs cash assistance plus employment services.
eligibility: Low-income families with children; work and program participation rules apply.
provides: Time-limited cash assistance, employment services and supportive benefits.
access: Apply through Mecklenburg Department of Community Resources.
caveat: Generally not available to childless adults; sanctions and time limits apply.

name: Common Wealth Charlotte
referralTrigger: A young adult needs budgeting, credit repair, banking access, debt planning or a safe small-dollar loan option.
eligibility: Charlotte-area residents; specific products/services have eligibility rules.
provides: Free financial counseling, workshops, safe banking access, credit guidance and eligible 0% loans after counseling.
access: Call or schedule a financial counseling session.
caveat: Loans are not automatic; participation and underwriting criteria apply.

name: Child Care Resources Inc. — Child Care Subsidy Support
referralTrigger: A parenting young adult needs affordable child care to work, attend school or training.
eligibility: Families meeting income, activity and child-age criteria; waitlists may apply.
provides: Help understanding and applying for child-care subsidy plus child-care search support.
access: Call the subsidy information line or use the website.
caveat: Subsidy funding and waitlists fluctuate; child-care placement is separate from subsidy approval.

name: Social Security — SSI / SSDI
referralTrigger: A young adult has a documented disability that substantially limits work and may qualify for federal income support.
eligibility: Federal disability, work-credit and financial criteria apply.
provides: Monthly disability income and potential connection to health coverage.
access: Apply through the Social Security Administration; gather medical and work documentation.
caveat: Applications are evidence-heavy and often denied initially; legal assistance may be useful for appeals.

name: Teen Health Connection
referralTrigger: A young person needs adolescent/young-adult primary care, behavioral health, nutrition or health education in one setting.
eligibility: Generally ages 11–25.
provides: Integrated medical and behavioral-health care tailored to adolescents and young adults.
access: Call for an appointment.
caveat: Insurance, sliding-fee and service eligibility should be confirmed when scheduling.

name: Care Ring Low-Cost Clinic
referralTrigger: An uninsured or underinsured adult needs affordable primary care.
eligibility: Adults meeting the clinic's service and financial criteria.
provides: Low-cost primary care, chronic-disease management and care coordination.
access: Call for eligibility and an appointment.
caveat: Not an emergency clinic; appointment availability varies.

name: Charlotte Community Health Clinic
referralTrigger: An uninsured, underinsured or Medicaid-covered person needs primary, dental or behavioral care.
eligibility: Open to community patients; discount eligibility is based on income and household size.
provides: Primary care, dental, behavioral health and pharmacy-related support.
access: Call for a new-patient appointment and ask about the discount program.
caveat: Appointment availability and service mix differ by location.

name: C.W. Williams Community Health Center
referralTrigger: A young adult needs affordable primary care through a federally qualified health center.
eligibility: Community patients; sliding-fee eligibility depends on income and documentation.
provides: Primary care and related health services regardless of ability to pay.
access: Call to establish care and ask about sliding-fee documentation.
caveat: Bring income/insurance information; specialty access may require referral.

name: Camino Health Center
referralTrigger: A Spanish-speaking or immigrant young adult needs culturally responsive primary care, behavioral health, wellness or food support.
eligibility: Community patients, especially uninsured/underinsured Latino families; program-specific criteria apply.
provides: Bilingual primary care, behavioral health, wellness education and food pantry support.
access: Contact Camino and request the appropriate service.
caveat: Some services may be limited to established health-center patients.

name: Mecklenburg Free and Low-Cost Clinic Directory
referralTrigger: FARM127 needs to compare multiple safety-net clinics by location and service.
eligibility: Eligibility varies by clinic.
provides: County list of free and low-cost medical, dental and specialty-care providers.
access: Use the directory, then call the selected clinic to verify intake.
caveat: Directory listings do not guarantee a provider is accepting new patients.

name: Mecklenburg Public Health — HIV/STI Testing and Treatment
referralTrigger: A young adult needs confidential HIV/STI testing, treatment or prevention counseling.
eligibility: Community members; service costs and appointment rules depend on test/treatment needs.
provides: HIV/STI testing, treatment, education and referral.
access: Call 704-432-TEST for testing help or 704-336-6500 for clinic appointments.
location: Mecklenburg County public-health clinics and community sites.
caveat: Walk-in and appointment procedures can change; call for current instructions.

name: RAO Community Health — HIV/STI Services
referralTrigger: A young adult needs free rapid HIV, hepatitis C or syphilis testing, PrEP or HIV-related care.
eligibility: Community members; some free services are limited to Mecklenburg residents.
provides: Testing, treatment linkage, PrEP and HIV supportive services.
access: Call or schedule through RAO Community Health.
caveat: Clinic schedules and free-service eligibility vary.

name: Planned Parenthood — Charlotte Health Center
referralTrigger: A young adult needs reproductive health care, contraception, pregnancy testing or STI services.
eligibility: Patients seeking covered services; fees and consent rules depend on service and age.
provides: Sexual and reproductive health services, including STI testing and treatment.
access: Call or book through the Charlotte Health Center.
caveat: Services, costs and insurance participation should be confirmed before the visit.

name: Care Ring Nurse-Family Partnership
referralTrigger: A first-time parent with limited resources needs home-visiting support during pregnancy and early childhood.
eligibility: First-time mothers meeting pregnancy timing, income and service-area criteria.
provides: Nurse home visits, prenatal/parenting education, health support and connection to resources.
access: Call or text for eligibility screening.
caveat: Enrollment must occur during pregnancy and capacity may be limited.

name: NAMI Charlotte
referralTrigger: A young adult or supporter needs mental-health education, peer/family support or crisis-resource guidance.
eligibility: Programs vary; many are free and open to people affected by mental illness.
provides: Support groups, education, advocacy and crisis-resource information.
access: Use the website to find a current group or program.
caveat: NAMI is not a crisis-response or clinical-treatment provider.

name: Anuvia Prevention & Recovery Center
referralTrigger: A young adult needs substance-use assessment, detox, outpatient or residential treatment.
eligibility: Adolescents and adults; clinical, payer and program criteria apply.
provides: Prevention, assessment, detoxification, residential and outpatient substance-use treatment.
access: Call the main line for assessment; use the detox line for withdrawal-management intake.
caveat: Level of care is determined clinically; bed availability and payment coverage vary.

name: McLeod Centers for Wellbeing
referralTrigger: A young adult needs evidence-based substance-use treatment, including outpatient or medication-assisted care.
eligibility: Adolescents/adults depending on program; clinical and payer criteria apply.
provides: Substance-use assessment and treatment across multiple levels of care.
access: Call for screening and the appropriate Charlotte-area program.
caveat: Program openings, insurance and medication-treatment criteria vary.

name: Time Out Youth — Counseling and Support
referralTrigger: An LGBTQ+ youth or young adult needs affirming counseling, groups, case support or community.
eligibility: LGBTQ+ youth and young adults; age range varies by service, generally through age 24.
provides: Free/low-cost counseling, support groups, case management, community and practical services.
access: Contact Time Out Youth for intake and the current service calendar.
caveat: Not every service is available to every age; housing and therapy may have separate waitlists.

name: NCWorks NextGen — Charlotte Works
referralTrigger: A young adult needs career coaching, paid work experience, training or help overcoming barriers to employment.
eligibility: Generally ages 16–24 with one or more employment/education barriers; program eligibility applies.
provides: No-cost career planning, training, credentials, supportive services and work-based learning.
access: Complete a NextGen interest/intake form through Charlotte Works or Central Piedmont.
caveat: Eligibility and funding-supported services require documentation; enrollment is not instant.

name: NCWorks Career Centers — Charlotte Works
referralTrigger: Any job seeker needs resume help, job-search support, workshops or connection to employers.
eligibility: Job seekers; some funded training programs have additional eligibility.
provides: Free career-center services, computers, workshops, job matching and training navigation.
access: Visit or contact a local NCWorks Career Center.
caveat: Training funds and program slots are limited; general career services remain free.

name: Central Piedmont — Finish High School (GED/HiSET)
referralTrigger: A young adult needs a high-school equivalency credential.
eligibility: Adults and eligible minors under program rules; placement/orientation requirements apply.
provides: Free preparation classes for GED or HiSET and adult high-school options.
access: Complete the Central Piedmont orientation/enrollment steps.
caveat: Testing fees and class schedules may vary even when instruction is free.

name: Central Piedmont — College and Career Readiness
referralTrigger: A young adult needs foundational academic, English-language, adult high-school or transition-to-college support.
eligibility: Program-specific eligibility and placement requirements.
provides: Adult education, English-language learning, high-school completion and career/college transition.
access: Follow Central Piedmont's CCR enrollment process.
caveat: Course locations, formats and start dates vary.

name: Goodwill Industries of the Southern Piedmont — Charlotte Career Center
referralTrigger: A young adult needs hands-on job search help, computer access, training enrollment or career coaching.
eligibility: Open career-center services; individual training programs have separate criteria.
provides: Resume/job-search help, computers, career coaching and access to skills training.
access: Visit the Charlotte Career Center or review the training calendar.
caveat: Course demand and enrollment windows vary.

name: Urban League of Central Carolinas
referralTrigger: A young adult wants no-cost occupational training and job placement support.
eligibility: Program-specific age, education and income criteria may apply.
provides: Training pathways including skilled trades, technology, customer service and healthcare-related programs.
access: Contact the Urban League and request current program enrollment information.
caveat: Course offerings, prerequisites and cohorts change.

name: Road to Hire
referralTrigger: A young adult wants paid training, mentorship and a pathway into a technical or professional career.
eligibility: Young adults meeting the current cohort's age, education and employment criteria.
provides: Paid training, professional development, mentorship and employer connections/apprenticeships.
access: Review current programs and apply during an open cohort.
caveat: Cohort eligibility and recruiting periods change; verify the current program before referring.

name: Year Up United — Charlotte
referralTrigger: A young adult wants structured job training, internship experience and employer access.
eligibility: Young adults meeting the Charlotte program's current age, education and work-authorization criteria.
provides: Career training, coaching, internship and job-placement support.
access: Attend an information session and complete the application.
caveat: Cohorts are competitive and time-bound; confirm current age and enrollment criteria.

name: Mecklenburg County — More Than a Job NC
referralTrigger: FARM127 needs a county-curated list of free job-driven training providers.
eligibility: Eligibility varies by partner program.
provides: Connections to free workforce training through partners such as Goodwill and Urban League.
access: Review the listed partners and apply with the relevant training provider.
caveat: This is a referral page, not a separate guaranteed-benefit program.

name: NC Employment and Independence for People with Disabilities (Vocational Rehabilitation)
referralTrigger: A young adult with a disability needs help preparing for, obtaining or keeping employment.
eligibility: A physical, mental, intellectual or sensory disability that creates a substantial barrier to employment; formal eligibility assessment required.
provides: Vocational counseling, training, job placement, assistive support and independent-living services.
access: Request services through the state EIPD office.
caveat: Eligibility and an individualized employment plan are required; services are not general cash assistance.

name: Charlotte Mecklenburg Library — College & Career Prep
referralTrigger: A young adult needs free online learning, resume tools, test preparation or library-based career resources.
eligibility: Library card/access requirements apply to some digital tools.
provides: Career, college, test-prep, technology and learning resources.
access: Use the Digital Branch or ask a library staff member for help.
caveat: Not a case-management or placement program; resource availability depends on library subscriptions.

name: Dress for Success Charlotte
referralTrigger: A low-income woman needs interview clothing, a work wardrobe and job-readiness support.
eligibility: Women referred through partner agencies or meeting current intake rules.
provides: Interview/employment styling, career coaching, financial education and professional development.
access: Request referral/intake instructions before visiting.
caveat: Services are designed for women and often require a referral appointment.

name: UNC Charlotte Niner Needs
referralTrigger: A currently enrolled UNC Charlotte student needs food, housing, transportation, technology, legal or emergency support.
eligibility: Current UNC Charlotte students; each support has its own criteria.
provides: Campus basic-needs navigation and emergency-support resources.
access: Use the Niner Needs site and contact the relevant campus office.
caveat: Only useful for enrolled students; emergency funds and services are limited.

name: CATS Fares and Passes
referralTrigger: A young adult needs to compare daily fares, passes and transit payment options.
eligibility: Public transit riders.
provides: Bus and light-rail fare information, passes and payment guidance.
access: Use the official fare page and the current CATS payment method.
caveat: Fares and pass products can change; verify before budgeting.

name: CATS Reduced Fare Transit IDs
referralTrigger: A rider with a qualifying disability, Medicare status or student category may be eligible for reduced fares.
eligibility: Qualifying riders under current CATS rules; documentation required.
provides: Reduced-fare identification and discounted transit fares.
access: Review documentation and apply for the appropriate Transit ID.
caveat: Not all low-income adults qualify; approval is category-based.

name: Mecklenburg Transportation System (MTS)
referralTrigger: An eligible resident needs non-emergency medical or human-services transportation.
eligibility: Medicaid beneficiaries and other qualifying residents based on age, disability or program status.
provides: Scheduled non-emergency medical and eligible general transportation.
access: Call for eligibility and trip scheduling; Medicaid members may also need health-plan authorization.
caveat: Advance scheduling and eligibility verification are required; not an on-demand ride service.

name: Charlotte Center for Legal Advocacy
referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs civil legal help involving benefits, housing, health care, immigration, taxes or expunction.
eligibility: Low-income residents and issue-specific service criteria.
provides: Free civil legal advocacy, advice and representation in selected matters.
access: Call the intake line or use Get Help; Spanish intake is available.
caveat: The organization cannot accept every case; legal deadlines continue while intake is pending.

name: Legal Aid of North Carolina
referralTrigger: A low-income young adult needs help with eviction, domestic violence, consumer issues, benefits or another civil legal problem.
eligibility: Low-income North Carolina residents; issue and conflict screening apply.
provides: Free civil legal information, advice and representation in eligible cases.
access: Apply online or call the statewide helpline.
caveat: High demand means not every eligible applicant receives representation.

name: Mecklenburg County Office of Vital Records
referralTrigger: A young adult needs a Mecklenburg birth or death certificate for identification, benefits, school or employment.
eligibility: Eligible applicants under state vital-record rules; identification and fees apply.
provides: Certified vital records.
access: Order online, by mail or in person using the county's instructions.
caveat: Only records in the office's jurisdiction are available; fees and ID requirements apply.

name: Safe Alliance — Victim Assistance and Sexual Assault Services
referralTrigger: A survivor needs crisis counseling, court advocacy, sexual-assault support or help navigating protective options.
eligibility: Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault or related victimization.
provides: 24/7 hotline, hospital accompaniment, counseling, court advocacy and safety planning.
access: Call the Greater Charlotte Hope Line.
caveat: Call 911 for immediate danger; legal representation may require referral to a legal-services provider.

name: Mecklenburg County Re-Entry Services
referralTrigger: A young adult recently released from incarceration needs employment, education, identification or service coordination.
eligibility: Generally Mecklenburg residents within one year of release; confirm current criteria.
provides: Re-entry case management, employment preparation, education and community-service connections.
access: Call the Re-Entry Services office for screening.
caveat: Eligibility is tied to justice involvement and release timing.

name: Center for Community Transitions
referralTrigger: A person affected by incarceration needs re-entry employment, family support or transition services.
eligibility: People with current/former justice-system involvement and their families; program criteria vary.
provides: Employment readiness, re-entry support and family-focused programs.
access: Contact the organization for the appropriate program intake.
caveat: Programs serve specific justice-involved populations; verify fit before referral.

name: National Human Trafficking Hotline
referralTrigger: A young adult may be experiencing labor or sex trafficking, exploitation or coercive control.
eligibility: Anyone seeking help or reporting a concern.
provides: 24/7 confidential safety planning, crisis support and connection to local services.
access: Call, text or use online chat; call 911 for immediate danger.
caveat: Hotline staff coordinate options but cannot guarantee immediate housing or law-enforcement response.

name: Hope for Justice — North Carolina Regional Center
referralTrigger: A trafficking survivor needs trauma-informed case management and longer-term support.
eligibility: Survivors meeting program criteria; confirm geographic and program eligibility.
provides: Trauma-informed advocacy, case management and connection to housing, health and legal resources.
access: Contact the North Carolina regional program for screening.
caveat: Capacity and referral criteria vary; this is not a 24/7 emergency hotline.

name: Smart Start of Mecklenburg County
referralTrigger: A parenting young adult needs early-childhood, parenting or child-development resources.
eligibility: Families and caregivers of young children; program eligibility varies.
provides: Parent education, early-childhood navigation and connections to family supports.
access: Use the families/caregivers resource page or contact Smart Start.
caveat: Smart Start coordinates and funds multiple programs; availability depends on the specific partner.

name: Disability Rights & Resources
referralTrigger: A young adult with a disability needs independent-living skills, advocacy, benefits navigation or accessibility support.
eligibility: People with disabilities; specific services may have geographic or program criteria.
provides: Independent-living skills, advocacy, transportation guidance, budgeting and employment-related support.
access: Contact the Center for Independent Living and request an intake.
caveat: This is an independent-living and advocacy organization, not residential care or emergency assistance.
